texts.preamble: Vishnu vs The Depot Manager on 14 October, 2022 Author: Pradeep Singh Yerur Bench: Pradeep Singh Yerur In The High Court Of Karnataka Kalaburagi Bench Dated This The 14 Th Day Of October, 2022 Before The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Singh Yerur Mfa No.202371/2017 (Mv-I) Between: Vishnu S/O Ramgopal Doddamani Age: 11 Years, R/G Of Natural Mother Smt. Padmamma W/O Ramgopal R/O Kodla Cros Sedam, Tq: Sedam, Dist: Kalaburagi-584101 ...Appellant (By Sri : Babu H Metagudda, Advocate) And: The Depot Manager Apsrtc Tandur(Vehicle No.Ap-11-Z-5788) Respondent (By Sri : S.V.Deshmukh, Advocate ) *** Mfa Filed U/S. 173(1) Of Mv Act, By The Advocate For Appellant Praying That This Hon Ble Court To, A) Call For The Records In Mvc No.1254/2015 On The File Of The Senior Civil Judge And Mact, Sedam. B)Allow This Appeal And Modify The Judgment And Award Dated 26.09.2017 Passed In Mvc No.1254/2015 By The Senior Civil Judge And Mact, Sedam, And Enhancing The Compensation From Rs.7,00,000/- With 6% Interest Pa To Rs.14,99,000/- With 12% Pa Interest. This Appeal Coming On For Final Hearing This Day, The Court Passed The Following: 2 Vishnu vs The Depot Manager on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43625540/ 1 Judgment
texts.facts: Unfortunate tale of minor child Vishnu, aged about 9 years, who met with an accident, suffered amputation of right leg, approached this Court in this appeal aggrieved by judgment and award dated 26.09.2017 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Sedam (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal' for brevity) in MVC No.1254/2015. The appellant, minor child Vishnu, represented by his mother and natural guardian, is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation on the ground that the Tribunal has awarded meager and inadequate compensation. 2. Young and energetic minor child Vishnu, aged about 9 years, who was returning from his school on 19.09.2015 at about 11.00am, unmindful of the fact and consequences that would occur on the said date and time which would turn around his life up side down and create an unexpected vaccume in remaining part of his life. While crossing the road to go to his house and immediately to play with his parents and his peer group, at that time APSRTC bus bearing Registration No.AP-11 / Z-5788 came from VCF factory driven by the driver of the bus in a high speed and rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety, without consideration of life and consequences of the minor child Vishnu, who was crossing the road after alighting from the school bus, dashed against him. 3. Due to the said impact, minor child Vishnu fell down on the road and bus ran over the right thigh of the minor child Vishnu, wherein minor child Vishnu sustained grievous injuries. Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Sedam. On initial diagnosis the Doctor advised that the minor child Vishnu be shifted for better and higher treatment to any other hospital. Accordingly, they shifted the minor child Vishnu to Kamareddy Hospital, Kalaburagi. Pursuant to the accident a criminal case came to be registered in Cr. No. 229/2015 before the Sedam Police Station against the driver of offending bus. 4. It is an unfortunate tale of the mother of the minor child Vishnu, who represents him as natural guardian, that the minor child Vishnu was absolutely hale and healthy prior to the accident and most cheerful boy with enormous energy and world ahead of him to be conquered, has lost his entire right leg due to the rash and negligent manner of driving and inhuman act of the driver of the bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation. The unfortunate mother unable to bear the trauma herself and that of the minor child Vishnu filed a claim petition seeking compensation from the respondent - Corporation. 5. On issuance of notice to the respondent - Corporation, objection statement came to be filed, inter alia, denying the averments made in the claim petition and pleaded that it was the fault of the minor child Vishnu himself, who crossed the road without taking due care by looking left and right of the road and ran across and thereby got himself injured in a busy road and it is not a rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation. It is also pleaded by the respondent - Corporation that though the minor child Vishnu has lost his right limb, he is only entitled to compensation as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, THE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY Vishnu vs The Depot Manager on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43625540/ 2 LIMITED AND OTHERS, reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396. It is further pleaded that the minor child Vishnu would not be entitled to exorbitant compensation sought for by the mother in the claim petition and sought for dismissal of the same. 6. On the basis of the pleadings the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration. 7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the mother of the minor child Vishnu examined herself as PW1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P13. She also examined the Doctor as PW2. On the other hand, the respondent - Corporation examined its Manager as RW1, but no documents were marked on their behalf.
texts.arguments: 9. Being aggrieved by the meager compensation amount awarded, claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation. 10. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for appellant-claimant - minor child Vishnu, represented by his mother and natural guardian that the Tribunal has erred in awarding meager compensation and has not taken into consideration the material evidence both oral and documentary thereby causing miscarriage of justice to the claimant. He further contends that the Tribunal has not at all applied its mind in awarding compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case wherein the minor child Vishnu, loaded with energy and enthusiasm, has lost his right leg due to the rash and negligent manner of driving by the driver of the bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation. 11. Learned Counsel for appellant - claimant further submits that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing proper income for arriving at calculation for assessing future income and has awarded global compensation of Rs.5,000/- per month towards loss of future income in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MALLIKARJUNA, stated supra. He further disagrees with the finding and calculation arrived at by the Tribunal and seeks enhancement of compensation. 12. Learned Counsel for appellant - claimant further contends that the Tribunal has lost sight of the facts and circumstances of the present case and has failed to award compensation under the head loss of marriage prospects; compensation towards future medical expenses; just and reasonable compensation under pain and suffering and compensation under the head attendant charges for the remaining part of the life of the appellant - claimant. 13. Learned Counsel for the appellant - claimant further contends that the Tribunal has committed serious error in not adding future prospects towards loss of future earning. On all these ground he contends that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation commensurate to the injuries sustained by the minor child Vishnu. On these grounds he seeks to allow this appeal and enhance the compensation in a reasonable manner. Vishnu vs The Depot Manager on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43625540/ 3 14. Learned Counsel for appellant - claimant relies on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of KAJAL Vs JAGADISH CHAND AND OTHERS reported in 2020 KANT MAC 489 (SC). 15. Per contra, learned Counsel Sri Deshmuk appearing on behalf of respondent - Corporation vehemently contends that the judgment and award of the Tribunal is just and reasonable and the Tribunal has considered all the material evidence both oral and documentary and has kept in mind magnitude of the injuries suffered by the minor child Vishnu and has taken all precautions and care while awarding just and reasonable compensation for the injuries sustained by the minor child Vishnu. 16. Learned Counsel for the respondent - Corporation further contends that the Tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation under other heads, which does not call for interference. He further contends that the Tribunal has properly considered the disability at 85% based on the evidence adduced by PW2 - Doctor to the whole body and has accordingly granted suitable compensation in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MALLIKARJUNA, stated supra. Learned Counsel sustains the order of the Tribunal by contending that the Tribunal has not lost sight of the fact that minor child Vishnu has lost his right leg and his entire life is ruined because of accident. However, He further contends that the Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation as a solace to the minor child Vishnu and his parents. On these grounds he seeks to dismiss the appeal filed by the appellant - claimant. 17. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and learned counsel for respondent - Corporation, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are: i) Whether the Tribunal has awarded meager compensation, which calls for interference by this Court? ii) Whether the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation? iii) What order 18. It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 19.09.2015 around 11.00 a.m. when the minor child Vishnu was crossing the road after attending his school to go to his house, during which time the offending bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation dashed against him leading to unfortunate incident of accident due to which his right leg was amputated. 21. In such cases, where the minor child is involved in accident and get injured, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held in the case of MALLIKARJUNA, stated supra, so also, in the case of KAJAL, stated supra, as to how the Tribunal and this Court will have to deal with the matter. 24. As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kajal stated supra which was decided in the year 2020, the Hon'ble Apex Court has taken the minimum wages payable to a workmen as the basis of assessment of income for award of compensation. The Karnataka State Legal Services Committee has prescribed the income chart to arrive at standard assessment of income in cases where there is no proof of income produced by the claimant. Accordingly, the income in the present case has to be assessed at Rs.8,000/- per month rather than taking notional income at Rs.15,000/- per annum as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kajal Vishnu vs The Depot Manager on 14 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43625540/ 5 Therefore, an addition of 40% towards the income stated above would have to be awarded towards loss of future earning capacity as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680. 27. In a case on hand, where the minor child is involved in the road traffic accident the appropriate multiplier that would be applicable is 18 and in the present case the multiplier is taken at 18 as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121. 28. This analysis is fortified in the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kajal stated supra.
